fields.h1: Build a Permanent Makeup Consent Form for Brows, Lips and Liner
fields.hero_description: Describe your studio and the procedures on your menu. Emergent builds the permanent makeup consent form, then files each client's pigments and photos under the signature.
fields.features_heading: What a PMU Consent Record Keeps
fields.features_subheading: What the artist needs signed before the first stroke, and what the studio looks up when the client comes back.
fields.feature_1:
One form for every procedure

Let the client pick the procedure first. Microblading, lip blush and eyeliner each load their own risk statements, and a brow client never initials a line written about the eyes.
fields.feature_2:
Pigment and lot number per color

Record each pigment the artist mixes with the lot number printed on its bottle. FDA recall notices for contaminated inks name the affected lots, and one search finds who got them.
fields.feature_3:
Before and healed photos in order

Attach the before photo at booking and ask for healing photos on the days your artist picks. Every photo is dated and filed under its session, next to the consent it follows.
fields.feature_4:
Each risk initialed, MRI included

Write allergic reactions and MRI complications as separate statements with initials boxes. The FDA lists both as permanent makeup risks. Signing stays locked until each is initialed.
fields.feature_5:
One client history across visits

Keep a color refresh years later on the same record as the first session. The artist opens that history and sees earlier brow shapes and pigments before the next appointment.
fields.feature_6:
Code your studio keeps

Export the full source code to GitHub on paid plans. A developer can place the consent form inside your booking site and keep editing it there long after the first version ships.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Studios Run PMU Consent
fields.tab_content_1:
Before booking, the artist sees the old brow work

Marlow Brow Studio books microblading through a form that asks one question first: has the client had brow tattooing before? A yes asks for a photo of the old work and sends the form to artist Jess Alvarez. She confirms or declines the slot, and only a confirmed client gets the consent link.
fields.tab_content_2:
Lot numbers for both pigments, one search away

Kira Patel blends two pigments for most lip blush clients at Rosewell PMU. After each session she adds both pigment names and their lot numbers to the signed record. If a manufacturer recalls a lot, a search for that number lists every client it went into, with phone numbers for the calls.
fields.tab_content_3:
Healing photos, day by day, next to the consent

Eyeliner clients at Linden Beauty get an upload link by email on day 3 and day 10 after their session. Each photo they send is dated and filed under that session, beside the before photo and the signed consent. Artist Dana Reyes opens one record and sees the whole heal in order.
fields.tab_content_4:
For the touch-up, session one's record opens first

Six weeks after a first session, Marlow Brow Studio sends the touch-up form. It shows the brow shape and pigment from session one next to the healed photo, then asks the client only what has changed since. She signs a one-page touch-up consent, and it joins the original on her record.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a PMU Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the wording already exists in your artist's consultation. The form records that talk and the sessions that follow it.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pick the answers that need the artist
fields.howto_step_1_des: Sit with your artist and note what they tell every client before the first stroke: what the procedure does, how the color settles, what can go wrong, and what a touch-up covers. The consent form has to capture that conversation.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List each service on your menu, such as powder brows or lip blush. Give each one its own risk statements and screening questions, and let the client's first answer decide which set appears on screen.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide which answers send a form to the artist before the appointment holds, like earlier brow tattooing or recent lip filler. Name the person who gets the alert, and choose whether it arrives by email or in a Slack channel.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose what the artist adds once the client leaves, starting with each pigment used and its lot number from the bottle. Then set the days your studio asks for healing photos and who reviews them.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your consent wording and the review rules. Emergent builds the form and the client table, with photo uploads, from that prompt. Ask for changes in plain English, such as a Spanish version or a new service.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the consent link with each booking confirmation and email clients a PDF of what they signed. Emergent connects to any tool with an API, including the booking software your front desk already works in every day.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it, then have it reviewed
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book yourself as a microblading client with old brow work, then as a lip blush client, and open both records. Ask a lawyer who knows your area's body art rules to read the wording, because tattooing is regulated locally.

claims_to_source: Permanent makeup is a type of tattoo: a needle places colored ink in the skin to look like eyeliner, lip liner or eyebrows
Inks used for permanent makeup are regulated as cosmetics by the FDA, and no color additive is approved for injection into the skin
FDA lists allergic reactions and MRI complications among the risks of tattoos and permanent makeup, and reports swelling or burning in the area during an MRI
The practice of tattooing is regulated by local jurisdictions, not by the FDA
FDA recall advisories for contaminated tattoo inks identify the affected product lots
Microblading is a semi-permanent cosmetic tattooing procedure that uses a hand tool with a row of fine needles to make hair-like strokes
